READABILITY.evidence: API types have clear doc comments and names (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookieAttribute). The logic sits in its own consistent_hash.go and follows the plugin's naming. Only fragments of that file were visible, but nothing there is cryptic.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: Follows the plugin pattern: a dedicated consistent_hash.go, an IR built in constructor.go (+4 lines), a 44-line addition to merge.go and apply wiring in traffic_policy_plugin.go. Deepcopy and CRD come from make go-generate-apis. No debug leftovers.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Inputs are checked at the CRD boundary: MinLength/MaxLength/MaxItems markers, a CEL rule on the ttl format and a CEL rule for disable exclusivity. A bad ttl is reported as a policy error, not dropped. The MaxItems=16 bounds are validation markers, not magic constants.

C7-11-CASE1.evidence: Golden merged route shows hashPolicy unioned from route-hash-a and route-hash-b, deduped and re-sorted into header→cookie→queryParameter→filterState→sourceIp order. Metadata records consistentHash under merge.TrafficPolicy.gateway.kgateway.dev with both refs.

C7-11-CASE2.evidence: Golden route-hash-default yields a single connectionProperties sourceIp entry, and the disabled route has no hashPolicy (apply sets action.HashPolicy=nil). A CEL XValidation on ConsistentHash rejects other fields when disable is true and appears in the generated CRD YAML.
